scope: User-selected educational priorities, not an efficacy ranking or accreditation list. Taxonomy, chemistry mappings and detailed profiles require specialist review. Toxic/controlled entries are recognition education only.

plants.clinical: Small studies do not establish a general sleep benefit. Compare the exact product and outcome.
plants.safety: Related-plant allergies and reported warfarin interactions matter.

plants.clinical: Some peppermint-oil preparations have evidence for IBS symptoms; do not generalize to all mint products.
plants.safety: Oil can cause heartburn; menthol oil must not be applied to an infant’s face.

plants.clinical: Research suggests benefit for pregnancy-associated nausea; results for other nausea settings differ.
plants.safety: Adverse effects and medicine interactions need preparation-specific review.

plants.clinical: Clinical conclusions remain uncertain; different formulations are not interchangeable.
plants.safety: Liver injury has been reported with some enhanced-bioavailability products.

plants.clinical: Supplement studies suggest small effects on some cardiovascular risk markers, not proof of prevention of cardiovascular events.
plants.safety: Supplements may increase bleeding risk. Product and medicine review matters.

plants.clinical: Oral-oil research and aromatherapy research are separate; study limitations remain.
plants.safety: Review route, preparation and adverse effects rather than treating all aromatic products alike.

plants.clinical: Use the exact species and preparation in the EMA monograph. Traditional use is not equivalent to trial-proven efficacy.
plants.safety: Essential oil is not equivalent to the herb; preparation-specific restrictions need review.

plants.clinical: Only limited research is available; definitive clinical conclusions cannot be drawn.
plants.safety: Common sage contains thujone; large amounts or prolonged use may be unsafe.

plants.clinical: The cited assessment concerns sweet fennel fruit; it does not cover every fennel product.
plants.safety: Study preparation, allergy and age restrictions in the monograph; concentrated oils are not culinary equivalents.

plants.clinical: High-quality evidence does not clearly support licorice for a general health indication.
plants.safety: Glycyrrhizin can cause serious cardiovascular adverse effects; medicine interactions are important.

plants.clinical: Gel, latex and whole-leaf products have different evidence and risk profiles.
plants.safety: Oral latex is not equivalent to topical gel. Do not infer that a whole leaf is safe to consume.

plants.clinical: EMA assesses senna leaf for short-term occasional constipation; refer to the exact monograph.
plants.safety: Contraindications, electrolyte effects and inappropriate prolonged use require review.

plants.clinical: Ispaghula husk has preparation-specific medicinal uses; distinguish husk from whole seed.
plants.safety: Swallowing problems and obstruction risk are relevant. Learn the product-specific precautions without improvising administration advice.

plants.clinical: Leaf and oil are different preparations; consult the source’s exact scope.
plants.safety: Concentrated essential oils can be hazardous; this lesson does not teach ingestion or use.

plants.clinical: EMA assesses particular rosemary-leaf preparations under a traditional-use framework.
plants.safety: Do not transfer the monograph to arbitrary oils or supplements.

plants.clinical: Liver-disease trial results are conflicting or too limited for firm conclusions.
plants.safety: Composition, microbial contamination and adulteration are relevant quality concerns.

plants.clinical: NCCIH finds no conclusive benefit for a health condition; prevention of dementia has not been demonstrated.
plants.safety: Bleeding and interaction risks require medicine review; leaf extracts and raw seeds are not equivalent.

plants.clinical: Evidence suggests usefulness for some mild-to-moderate depression settings, but product and comparator matter.
plants.safety: Can interact dangerously with many medicines. Interaction review is central to this record.

plants.clinical: Evidence for sleep problems is inconsistent; formulations differ.
plants.safety: Sedative combinations and uncertain long-term safety require review.

plants.clinical: Products vary by species, part and extraction. Do not treat them as a single intervention.
plants.safety: Allergic reactions can occur; investigate the exact preparation and clinical context.

plants.clinical: Studies are often small and variable; not every promoted use is established.
plants.safety: Sleep effects, blood-glucose effects and interactions need product-specific review.

plants.clinical: Some small studies concern stress and sleep; long-term efficacy and safety are not established.
plants.safety: Liver injury reports, pregnancy avoidance and thyroid-related concerns require review.

plants.clinical: The cited LiverTox record is not a comprehensive efficacy review; broad therapeutic claims are not established here.
plants.safety: LiverTox describes tolerability but does not establish safety for every preparation or population.

plants.clinical: Evidence for diabetes and milk supply is limited or mixed; food use is not proof of supplement efficacy.
plants.safety: Allergy, lowered blood glucose and pregnancy-related concerns need review.

plants.clinical: Evidence does not clearly establish cinnamon for a health condition. Verify which species was studied.
plants.safety: Cassia and Ceylon cinnamon differ; coumarin exposure is a product/species issue.

plants.part: Flower buds; oil is a separate preparation
plants.clinical: The cited EMA record concerns clove oil, not clinical validation of every clove preparation.
plants.safety: Concentrated oil needs a distinct safety assessment; no home-use procedure is supplied.

plants.clinical: Beverage studies and concentrated-extract studies should not be conflated.
plants.safety: Some green-tea extracts have been associated with liver injury; caffeine adds separate risks.

plants.clinical: The FDA source concerns caffeine exposure and safety, not a therapeutic claim for coffee.
plants.safety: Individual sensitivity and total caffeine from all sources matter.

plants.clinical: The cited chemical-exposure monograph is not evidence that cacao treats disease.
plants.safety: Food composition and a purified alkaloid are different exposure contexts.

plants.clinical: EMA describes traditional use of specific leaf preparations; trial evidence is limited.
plants.safety: Review biliary contraindications and related-plant allergy in the monograph.

plants.clinical: Very little human research is available; historical use is not proof of benefit.
plants.safety: Distinguish food exposure from supplements and review allergies and interactions.

plants.clinical: Evidence is inconsistent; the NCCIH overview covers several species and preparations.
plants.safety: Cardiovascular symptoms and medicine interactions need professional review; not a substitute for proven care.

plants.clinical: Some standardized seed-extract studies concern venous insufficiency. These findings do not apply to raw seeds.
plants.safety: Raw seeds, bark, flowers and leaves are unsafe orally; standardized products are distinct.

plants.clinical: Large studies and reviews find little or no benefit for urinary symptoms from prostate enlargement.
plants.safety: Study tolerability and population-specific precautions; efficacy cannot be assumed from popularity.

plants.clinical: Some evidence concerns prevention of recurrent UTIs in selected populations. It is not a treatment for an existing UTI.
plants.safety: Do not delay diagnosis or established treatment of suspected infection.

plants.part: Leaf; oil is a different material
plants.clinical: EMA’s leaf assessment is not an assessment of olive oil or every leaf supplement.
plants.safety: Review the exact leaf monograph; food-oil evidence cannot be transferred automatically.

plants.clinical: The cited LiverTox entry concerns margosa oil toxicity, not an efficacy endorsement for neem.
plants.safety: Neem seed oil has caused serious poisoning; plant parts and products cannot be treated as interchangeable.

plants.clinical: Small studies suggest possible effects for some symptoms, but high-quality evidence is insufficient.
plants.safety: Preparation-specific safety and composition require review; a resin is not a single compound.

plants.clinical: EMA’s traditional-use assessment is preparation-specific, not proof for general systemic use.
plants.safety: Study restrictions and allergy; no ingestion or formulation recipe is included.

plants.clinical: The EMA overview covers several Salix species. Do not infer species-specific trial efficacy for S. alba.
plants.safety: Review salicylate-related restrictions and exact species/preparation in the monograph.

plants.clinical: A dangerous plant’s pharmaceutical history is not evidence for home treatment.
plants.safety: HIGHLY TOXIC: all parts may be deadly if swallowed. Observation only.

plants.clinical: Recognition and toxicology only; no therapeutic use of the garden plant is taught.
plants.safety: HIGHLY TOXIC. Poisonous berries and other parts must never be consumed or prepared.

plants.clinical: Distinguish regulated pharmaceutical medicines from a raw plant; no clinical use of a plant preparation is taught.
plants.safety: CONTROLLED-MATERIAL CONTEXT. Recognition and history only; no cultivation, harvesting, preparation or use instructions. Rules depend on jurisdiction.

plants.clinical: Study the pharmaceutical history of quinine. Bark is not a substitute for a licensed antimalarial medicine.
plants.safety: Potentially serious toxicity; no self-treatment or raw-bark preparation is taught.

plants.clinical: Vinca-derived oncology medicines are standardized drugs; the plant is not a cancer treatment.
plants.safety: TOXIC. Observation and drug-discovery education only.

plants.clinical: Paclitaxel is an oncology medicine with specific approved indications; this does not authorize use of yew material.
plants.safety: TOXIC PLANT CONTEXT. No collection, extraction or self-treatment.

plants.clinical: Modest short-term supplement effects did not outweigh serious risks.
plants.safety: Serious cardiovascular and neurological harms. US ephedrine-alkaloid dietary supplements are banned; this is not a global legal classification.

plants.focus: Castor oil versus highly toxic seeds
plants.clinical: Pharmaceutical oil and poisonous seeds are different materials; no home processing is taught.
plants.safety: HIGHLY TOXIC SEEDS. Never consume, crush, prepare or use seeds as a remedy.

plants.clinical: Study historical pharmaceutical use; the linked hazard assessment is not a therapeutic endorsement.
plants.safety: Potent pharmacological and adverse effects. No raw-root remedy or dosing is taught.

plants.clinical: A regulated medicine containing colchicine is not interchangeable with a toxic plant.
plants.safety: HIGHLY TOXIC. Recognition and medicine-safety education only; never consume or prepare the plant.

modules.title: Everyday medicinal plants
modules.activity: Connect familiar common names with scientific names and study materials.

modules.title: Phytochemical foundations
modules.activity: Match the selected study marker to a plant; separate material identity from efficacy.

modules.title: Clinical herbal products
modules.activity: Investigate product-specific evidence and challenge unsupported clinical claims.

modules.title: Pharmaceutical natural products
modules.activity: Trace the difference between a plant, an extract and a regulated medicine. Not every member has an approved drug.

modules.title: Toxicology & safety
modules.focus: Hazards, adverse effects and material distinctions
modules.activity: Recognize why identity, part, preparation and clinical context change risk. Membership is not a toxicity ranking.
